title: AuthZ Onboarding & KMS/Encryption Review with EmberTech
summary: Redwood and EmberTech reviewed SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning flows, and RBAC/least-privilege design. Discussed encryption options including BYOK/KMS, HSM, audit log retention and data residency constraints. Agreed to share SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SCIM mapping template, and schedule a private deployment canary for perf/security testing.
topics: SAML metadata and IdP thumbprint exchange
SCIM attribute mapping and provisioning cadence
RBAC role matrix and least-privilege patterns
Audit logs retention and SIEM integration
Data residency and export controls; hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs
next_steps: Alex to send SOC 2 Type II report, ISO27001 summary, and penetration test summary (by 2027-02-12)
Maya to share SCIM attribute mapping template and role matrix example (by 2027-02-15)
Schedule 2-hour canary run for private deployment with EmberTech infra team (target week of 2027-02-22)
Samir to provide SAML metadata and IdP contact and indicate required user attributes (by 2027-02-11)
action_items: Alex Moran - Send SOC 2 Type II pack and ISO summary - 2027-02-12
Maya Chen - Draft SCIM mapping & least-privilege role matrix - 2027-02-15
Samir Khan - Provide SAML metadata XML and IdP contact - 2027-02-11
Jordan Patel - Confirm data residency region constraints and allowed egress - 2027-02-14
transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2027-02-09
- Start time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Dir Eng, EmberTech), Priya Nair (Head of Security, EmberTech), Samir Khan (Cloud Architect, EmberTech), Lena Ortiz (Procurement)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC patterns for least privilege, and deep-dive on KMS/BYOK and audit logging. Customer had questions on key ownership, log export to Splunk, and whether Redwood supports per-tenant HSMs in private deployments.

[00:00] Alex Moran: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, should we do quick intros then jump into the KMS and SCIM stuff, um Maya will take the SAML flow and I can cover compliance artifacts.
[00:35] Jordan Patel: Hi, Jordan here. We're most interested in locking down who can call the inference endpoints and make sure we can audit every token usage, and also that keys never leave our control if possible.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Yes, plus we need to confirm log retention windows for SOC 2 and also any PII routing rules if data crosses regions.
[01:40] Maya Chen: Great. I'll start with the SAML/SSO screen flow at a high level - Redwood supports SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML, metadata XML upload and assertion consumer URLs are configurable per-tenant.
[02:05] Samir Khan: Quick question — do you also push user groups via the assertion or do you require SCIM?
[02:25] Maya Chen: You can do either. We accept group claims in SAML but for automated provisioning we strongly recommend SCIM so you can provision/deprovision users and role memberships. SCIM is optional but recommended for enterprise.
[03:00] Jordan Patel: SCIM sounds good. We have an HR feed so automating deprovisioning is a must. Show us the attribute map, like what names you need for username, email, role, team, etc.
[03:40] Maya Chen: Sure — on the template we ask for: userName, emails[0].value, displayName, active, groups, and a custom attribute for tenant_role. I'll share the spreadsheet after the call.
[04:20] Alex Moran: On the compliance side, we can share SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO27001 summary, also pen test executive summary. They are redacted in spots but should satisfy procurement.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: Procurement wants to see those yes, also the standard DPA language and SCCs for EU data.
[05:10] Priya Nair: Back to RBAC — we need least-privilege by default. How are permission scopes modeled in Redwood? Are they coarse-grained (admin/user) or more fine-grained?
[05:40] Diego Ruiz: We expose a role model: built-in roles (org admin, billing, observer) plus custom roles with fine-grained API permissions. You can create scoped roles for 'invoke-model', 'view-logs', 'manage-deployments' etc.
[06:10] Maya Chen: We recommend a small number of roles mapped to IdP groups, then a separate runtime policy for model-level controls. For example, a 'service' role might only have invoke rights against a single model alias.
[06:45] Jordan Patel: Can we enforce least privilege at token granularity? Like issue short-lived tokens tied to specific model scopes?
[07:05] Diego Ruiz: Yes — we support scoped API keys with TTLs. For high security, pair those with mTLS or VPC peering on private deployments.
[07:30] Priya Nair: Now the big one — KMS/BYOK. Do you allow us to bring our own key and rotate it, ideally with HSM-backed keys?
[07:55] Maya Chen: For Hosted API, we manage encryption at rest with provider KMS. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS — you can bring keys from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure KeyVault. HSM-backed keys are supported if your KMS/HSM offers that to the tenant.
[08:30] Samir Khan: Do we get key wrapping or do you see plaintext keys at any point?
[08:48] Diego Ruiz: We never handle raw plaintext Private keys. We exchange wrapped key blobs through the control plane during onboarding; the unwrapped key material only exists in your KMS/HSM. For hosted we hold the managed keys but you can ask for a dedicated key per account in dedicated deployments.
[09:20] Jordan Patel: How about rotation — can we rotate without downtime and revoke old sessions?
[09:40] Maya Chen: Rotation is designed to be rolling — you can schedule rotation through KMS then trigger a rewrap operation. Short-lived tokens mitigate session exposure; for active sessions we provide graceful rekeying with immediate revocation options if needed.
[10:20] Priya Nair: Audit logs — we need event-level logs for calls, who invoked which model, input hashes, and any admin changes. What retention and SIEM exports do you support?
[10:50] Alex Moran: We provide tenant-level audit logs with configurable retention. For Hosted customers this defaults to 90 days; enterprise customers can purchase extended retention. We also have push integrations to Splunk, S3, BigQuery, and Datadog for archiving.
[11:30] Samir Khan: We want logs forwarded to our Splunk instance in IL for 3 years to meet internal policy — is that possible?
[11:50] Diego Ruiz: Yes, we can forward logs over TLS to your collector; for very long retention we recommend archiving to your S3 bucket in the correct region. For export controls/data residency we can ensure logs never cross region boundaries if on private deployment.
[12:25] Jordan Patel: Any chance of including request/response payloads in logs? We have concerns about PII — need to know whether Redwood masks or hashes sensitive fields automatically.
[12:45] Maya Chen: We avoid storing full user-provided inputs by default for Hosted; customers may opt-in to store inputs for debugging but we recommend hashing sensitive fields. In Private setups, you control retention and whether payloads are persisted. We can also provide redaction rules or a post-processing lambda to scrub PII before storing.
[13:20] Priya Nair: Regarding SOC 2 compliance gaps — do you have syslogs, SIEM alerting, and segregation of duties documented?
[13:40] Alex Moran: Yes, our SOC 2 covers access controls, change management, and monitoring. The report includes role segregation and change logs. I'll attach the executive summary and the controls matrix.
[14:10] Lena Ortiz: Procurement will need a summary mapping to our vendor risk questionnaire — typical milestone is to map control IDs to our questions.
[14:40] Alex Moran: We can provide a control mapping matrix.
[15:05] Samir Khan: One more infrastructure question — for private deployment, do you support per-tenant VPC peering and dedicated GPU pools?
[15:30] Diego Ruiz: Yes, Dedicated and Private support dedicated GPU pools and customer VPC peering. That is how we isolate network and instance-level layers.
[16:00] Jordan Patel: On the SAML side, we'll want to provision specific groups for 'model-invokers' and 'model-admins'. If SCIM provisioning can sync group membership automatically on hire/term, that solves majority of our IAM pain.
[16:30] Maya Chen: Exactly. The SCIM mapping sample ties SCIM groups to Redwood roles by group name. You can also include entitlements as a custom attribute if you prefer.
[17:00] Priya Nair: What about emergency access — break glass? If our IdP is down, can we still get emergency admin access?
[17:20] Diego Ruiz: We support emergency API keys with step-up authentication and time-limited TTLs. For Private deployments, there's an out-of-band admin console via bastion that can be constrained to certain IPs.
[17:55] Jordan Patel: Good. Procurement question — pricing for private with BYOK and extended log retention?
[18:10] Alex Moran: We'll include those line items in the quote. Private deployments with BYOK and 3-year log archiving typically land in our enterprise tier; I'll follow up with exact numbers.
[18:45] Samir Khan: Any compliance differences if we choose hosted with dedicated capacity vs Private?
[19:05] Maya Chen: Hosted dedicated capacity gives you predictable performance and tenant isolation at the software level, but the encryption keys are managed by Redwood unless you bring a dedicated key. Private gives you full control over networking and KMS. There's also SLA differences and network egress constraints.
[19:40] Priya Nair: For data residency, we need all inference traffic to stay in eu-west-1. Can Redwood guarantee that for hosted?
[20:00] Diego Ruiz: For hosted we route to regionally colocated clusters; we can route EU traffic to eu-west-1 clusters but for strict legal control we recommend Private in that region or a hosted arrangement with contractual region restrictions. We'll capture that in the DPA.
[20:35] Jordan Patel: On the RBAC matrix — will you share an example for mapping our IdP groups to Redwood roles?
[20:50] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll share a template with examples, e.g., 'ember-model-invoke' => invoke-model for model X, 'ember-admin' => org admin.
[21:15] Priya Nair: Any built-in attestation logs for admin actions like model rollouts and canary toggles? We need to audit who rolled a model and when.
[21:40] Diego Ruiz: Yes, deployment events are logged with actor, timestamp, and the diff of the rollout. Those show up in the audit stream and can be exported.
[22:05] Jordan Patel: From a threat model perspective, how do you protect the KV cache (the runtime memory with prompt contexts)? If someone compromised an instance is there risk of cross-tenant leakage?
[22:30] Maya Chen: KV caches are isolated per tenant and per worker process. We use memory isolation techniques and scrub memory on eviction. For additional isolation we recommend dedicated GPU pools. We also run fuzz tests and regression e2e checks on memory handling.
[23:05] Priya Nair: Can you provide results of recent penetration tests that cover model serving and mem-scrub?
[23:25] Alex Moran: We have an executive summary and remediation trackers. I'll include the pen test high-level findings; detailed reports can be shared under NDA if needed.
[24:00] Samir Khan: Operationally, if we use SCIM, what's the provisioning cadence? Real-time? Polling?
[24:15] Maya Chen: SCIM is typically event-driven push from IdP to Redwood; some IdPs poll depending on implementation. We support real-time provisioning via SCIM 2.0 with delta updates.
[24:50] Jordan Patel: For role changes, can we do attribute-based access, like mapping service tags to model scopes?
[25:10] Diego Ruiz: We support attribute-based rules in policies — you can have a rule that checks a team attribute or environment tag before allowing model invocation. It's fairly flexible.
[25:45] Priya Nair: Are there org-level guardrails to prevent accidental privilege escalation by delegated admins?
[26:05] Maya Chen: Yes. We have admin scopes and two-person approval for critical ops, and you can require MFA enforcement for certain role elevates. Those controls are in the console and exposed via API.
[26:35] Jordan Patel: Ok, let's talk timing — we want to run a private canary for inference latency and security posture. Ideally next week. What do you need from us?
[26:55] Alex Moran: We'll need Terraform creds or an infra contact to set up the private cluster, SAML metadata, and KMS access pattern (e.g., service principal). Diego will lead the infra onboarding.
[27:25] Diego Ruiz: We'll provide a step-by-step runbook. The typical canary includes 2 GPUs, identity config, and a synthetic traffic runner. We'll instrument audit logs and Splunk forwarding during the run.
[28:00] Jordan Patel: Perfect. Any blockers on our side?
[28:12] Samir Khan: We'll need a security review vetting the rewrap process and key exchange. Priya will confirm the legal NDA for pen test reports.
[28:35] Priya Nair: Also want to ensure the DPA includes restrictions on backups and third-party subprocessors.
[28:55] Alex Moran: We'll attach the current subprocessor list and DPA.
[29:20] Maya Chen: Quick note — for SCIM group naming best practices, avoid punctuation and keep groups stable names to avoid sync churn.
[29:45] Jordan Patel: Noted.
[30:00] -- Mid-call recap and shared links --
[30:05] Alex Moran: Recap — Alex will send compliance artifacts, Maya will send SCIM and RBAC template, Diego will own the infra runbook, Samir to provide SAML metadata. Target canary week of 2/22. Any objections?
[30:40] Jordan Patel: No objections, sounds good.
[31:05] Lena Ortiz: Procurement will expect cost line items, please follow up in writing.
[31:30] Alex Moran: Will do — expect pricing and a short SOW.
[32:00] -- deeper technical exchange --
[32:10] Priya Nair: A curiosity — do you maintain a key rotation history and prove key lineage in case of audit?
[32:35] Diego Ruiz: We maintain rotation logs with KMS key IDs, rotation timestamps, and public key fingerprints. For BYOK we rely on your KMS audit logs for full lineage but we keep references and manifest entries in our audit stream.
[33:05] Samir Khan: For incident response, how quickly can keys be revoked and new nodes reprovisioned?
[33:25] Maya Chen: With our automation you can revoke a key and reprovision within minutes in most cases, rewraps and cache invalidations are atomic across the fleet.
[33:55] Jordan Patel: Do you support role-based tokens for service accounts that are rotated automatically?
[34:15] Diego Ruiz: Yes, service accounts can get short-lived ephemeral tokens via our token service; rotations are automatic and we can integrate with your secret manager for lifecycle events.
[34:40] Priya Nair: Ok. Can you show the sample SCIM attribute mapping now?
[34:52] Maya Chen: (screen share) This is the sample CSV — username,email,active,groups,department,custom:tenant_role; mapping maps groups to Redwood roles.
[35:20] Jordan Patel: We'll need an additional attribute for 'allowed_models' per group — can that be passed as a JSON blob?
[35:45] Maya Chen: We accept a stringified JSON in a custom attribute or multiple entitlements attributes. We'll include examples.
[36:10] Samir Khan: On the Splunk forwarder — is the endpoint TLS auth only or do you support token-based auth?
[36:30] Diego Ruiz: We support mutual TLS to customer collectors and token-based HTTPS endpoints. mTLS is preferred for higher security.
[36:55] Priya Nair: Anything else on export controls — if we need a particular model to not leave the EU for legal reasons, can you pin model weights to EU-hosted infra?
[37:20] Maya Chen: For curated models we can pin inference to region-specific pools; for custom models you can deploy them to the region you control. We'll document that in the SOW.
[37:55] Jordan Patel: Great. Quick question on service accounts — can we have automated short-lived creds minted by our IdP?
[38:15] Diego Ruiz: We can integrate with OIDC and SAML assertion exchange to mint short-lived tokens; many customers use that for service-to-service auth.
[38:45] Samir Khan: For the canary, will you include a security checklist we need to close?
[39:00] Alex Moran: Yes — infra checklist, network allowlist, KMS config, SAML metadata, SCIM mapping, and test vectors. We'll provide that by EOD.
[39:30] Priya Nair: Can you commit to a remediation SLAs for critical vulnerabilities discovered during the canary?
[39:50] Diego Ruiz: We have an internal triage and customer severity SLAs. For critical issues we aim for immediate mitigation plans and patches within the agreed SLA window, we'll put that in the SOW.
[40:20] Jordan Patel: One last nit — ability to restrict model output logs from being used to train models in Redwood multi-tenant hosted setups? We need contractual guarantees.
[40:45] Alex Moran: We do not use customer input or outputs to train models unless explicitly opted-in. We'll provide a training-use policy clause in the DPA and contract.
[41:10] Jordan Patel: Excellent.
[41:30] -- final wrap up --
[41:35] Alex Moran: To summarize final asks: (1) EmberTech to provide SAML metadata and desired group naming; (2) Redwood to send SOC2/ISO and pen test executive summary; (3) Redwood to send SCIM mapping template and RBAC examples; (4) Set up canary next week.
[41:55] Lena Ortiz: We'll expect pricing and SOW.
[42:10] Jordan Patel: Priya will review the DPA, Samir will share the infra contacts for canary.
[42:35] Priya Nair: Thanks all. Any quick clarifications?
[42:50] Diego Ruiz: Nothing else from infra side.
[43:05] Maya Chen: I'll email the templates and keep the mapping lightweight.
[43:25] Alex Moran: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links to docs and a calendar invite for the canary.
[43:45] Jordan Patel: Thanks.
[44:00] -- end meeting --

Notes on transcript quality: occasional overlaps and a couple of misattributed speakers, some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., K V cache as KV cache, IdP vs I d p).
